s001: Agafay desert sunset, camel ride and dinner
s002: The desert is 45 minutes from Marrakech. Ride a camel across the stony hills of Agafay at sunset, with the snowy Atlas behind, then dinner at a camp.
s003: Agafay is not a sand desert but a wide landscape of bare, golden hills, and on clear days the High Atlas stands white behind it. It is the easiest way to feel the desert without a long drive. You are picked up in the afternoon, ride camels for about an hour at sunset, then have dinner at a camp before driving back to Marrakech.
s005: Views of the snowy High Atlas
s008: Pickup in Marrakech, mint tea at the camp, camel ride at sunset, dinner, and drive back.
s014: Your riad or hotel in Marrakech.
s015: Times move with the season, to match the sunset.
s016: Aït Benhaddou and Ouarzazate day trip
s017: Over the Tichka pass to the earth ksar of Aït Benhaddou and the kasbahs of Ouarzazate, the gateway to the desert.
s018: A long but spectacular day. The road climbs through Amazigh villages to the Tizi n’Tichka pass at 2,260 m, then drops to Aït Benhaddou, a fortified village of earth and straw on the old caravan route. A local guide takes you up through its lanes, then you continue to Ouarzazate and its kasbah before driving back over the mountains.
s021: Ouarzazate, the gateway to the desert
s023: Over the Tichka pass, guided visit of Aït Benhaddou, lunch, Ouarzazate, and back to Marrakech in the evening.
s025: A gentler way to reach Lake Ifni, from the south side of the Toubkal massif. Village life in Amsouzart and a night by the lake.
s026: Amsouzart sits on the southern side of the Toubkal massif, far from the busy Imlil trails. After a scenic drive you spend the first night in a village guesthouse, walk up the valley the next day to Lake Ifni and sleep by the water, then walk back down and drive to Marrakech. Moderate days, big landscapes and very few other walkers.
s027: Lake Ifni, the only high lake of the Toubkal massif
s028: A night in a family guesthouse in Amsouzart
s029: Quiet trails away from the crowds
s031: A long, beautiful drive to the south side of the massif. Afternoon walk around the village.
s033: Walk up the valley to the lake. Time to rest, swim if you dare, and watch the light change on the rock walls.
s035: Walk down to Amsouzart and drive back to Marrakech, arriving in the late afternoon.
s037: The best of both worlds in five days. Two days of walking from Imlil with nights in the mountains, then the road over the Atlas to the Merzouga dunes.
s038: Start where we live: two days of walking among the villages of the Imlil valleys, with a night in a guesthouse. Then the car takes you over the High Atlas to Aït Benhaddou, the Dades valley and Merzouga, where you ride camels into Erg Chebbi for a night at camp before driving back to Marrakech. Mountains, villages, kasbahs and dunes in one trip.
s039: Walk the Imlil valleys with a local guide
s040: Night in the Erg Chebbi dunes
s041: Mountains and desert in one trip
s043: Morning drive, then an afternoon walk around Aroumd. Dinner and night in Imlil.
s045: A full day over Tizi n’Tamatert and through the villages of the Imnane valley, back to the guesthouse.
s046: Over the Atlas to the Dades valley
s047: Tichka pass, Aït Benhaddou and the Valley of Roses to the Dades gorges.
s049: Todra gorge, then Merzouga and a camel ride at sunset to camp.
s050: Sunrise on the dunes and the long road back to Marrakech.
s051: Atlas three valleys and Imlil day trip
s052: An easy day in the mountains, with the village of Imlil as the highlight. Asni market town, Ouirgane, a short walk around Imlil and lunch with a view of Toubkal.
s053: Not a hike, a mountain day for everyone. You drive up the Moulay Brahim gorge to Asni, stop by the lake and hills of Ouirgane, then go up to Imlil for a gentle walk among walnut trees and earth houses, with tea in a village home. A good choice with children or older travellers.
s054: Imlil, at the foot of Toubkal
s058: Drive through the valleys with stops, a gentle walk around Imlil, lunch, and back to Marrakech.
s060: The blue town of the Rif mountains. A day of free wandering in Chefchaouen’s painted lanes, with a viewpoint walk to the Spanish mosque at sunset.
s061: About three and a half hours from Fes through olive groves and the Rif foothills. In Chefchaouen you have the day to explore the blue medina, the kasbah and the Outa el-Hammam square, and to walk up to the Spanish mosque for the view. Drive back to Fes in the evening.
s066: Drive to Chefchaouen, free day in the medina, viewpoint walk, drive back to Fes.
s067: Your riad or hotel in Fes.
s069: Sea air after the heat of Marrakech. The white-and-blue medina of Essaouira, its fishing port and ramparts, with a stop at an argan cooperative on the way.
s070: Essaouira is a calm, windy port town on the Atlantic, about three hours west of Marrakech. On the way you stop at a women’s argan oil cooperative, and if you are lucky you will see the famous goats in the argan trees. In town you have free time to walk the ramparts, watch the fishing boats come in and eat grilled fish at the port.
s071: A UNESCO-listed medina by the ocean
s072: Fresh grilled fish at the port
s075: Drive west with a stop at an argan cooperative, free day in Essaouira, drive back in the late afternoon.
s076: Your riad or hotel in Marrakech, or a central meeting point for shared trips.
s077: Essaouira is windy and cooler than Marrakech, even in summer. Bring a light jacket.
s079: The largest car-free medina in the world, with a licensed guide from Fes. Bou Inania madrasa, the Chouara tannery, Al-Qarawiyyin and the craftsmen’s alleys.
s080: Fes el-Bali has more than 9,000 lanes, and a good guide makes the difference between a maze and a story. You enter by the Blue Gate, visit the Bou Inania madrasa, pass the Al-Qarawiyyin mosque and university, watch the tanners at work from a terrace above Chouara, and walk through the metalworkers’ square. A full or half day, as you like.
s085: Blue Gate, Bou Inania, Al-Qarawiyyin, Chouara tannery and the craftsmen’s quarters.
s086: Your riad in Fes, or Bab Boujloud (the Blue Gate).
s087: Fes to Marrakech via the Merzouga desert, 3 days
s088: The best way to travel between Fes and Marrakech. Cedar forests of the Middle Atlas, a night in the Erg Chebbi dunes and the road of the kasbahs.
s089: Instead of the train, cross the country. You leave Fes through Ifrane and the cedar forests of the Middle Atlas, follow the Ziz valley down to the Sahara and ride camels to a camp in Erg Chebbi. Then the Todra and Dades gorges, Ouarzazate and the Tichka pass bring you to Marrakech. A 4-day version with more time on the way is possible on request.
s091: Cedar forests and Barbary macaques near Azrou
s092: A night in the Erg Chebbi dunes
s094: Via Ifrane, the cedar forest, Midelt and the Ziz valley to Merzouga. Camel ride at sunset and night at camp.
s096: Sunrise on the dunes, then west to the Todra gorge and the Dades valley.
s098: Through the Valley of Roses and Ouarzazate, a stop at Aït Benhaddou, and over the Tichka pass to Marrakech.
s100: The whole country in twelve days. Imperial cities, the blue town of Chefchaouen, the Sahara, the gorges and kasbahs, the High Atlas and Essaouira on the ocean.
s101: A private loop from Casablanca for travellers who want to see everything once. North to Rabat and Chefchaouen, then Fes and the Middle Atlas, south to the Merzouga dunes, west along the road of the kasbahs to Aït Benhaddou, a night in the mountains at Imlil, Marrakech and a final day by the sea in Essaouira. Your driver adapts the pace; every night is booked in advance.

s105: Ends on the ocean in Essaouira

s110: A slow day in the blue medina.
s112: The Roman ruins of Volubilis and Moulay Idriss on the way to Fes.

s118: Sunrise on the dunes, then the gorges.
s120: Valley of Roses, Ouarzazate and the ksar of Aït Benhaddou.
s122: Tichka pass, then up to Imlil for a walk and a night with mountain views.
s124: Down to Marrakech, guided afternoon in the medina.

s129: The Moroccan way to rest after a trek or a day in the souks. Steam, black soap, a full scrub with the kessa glove, then an argan oil massage.
s130: We book you into a clean, well-run hammam in the medina. An attendant takes you through the steam rooms, washes you with black soap and scrubs you head to toe, then you relax with mint tea before a massage with argan oil. Separate spaces for women and men; couples’ rooms on request.
s135: Steam, scrub, rest and a 45-minute massage.
s136: At the hammam in the medina (address sent with the booking).
s138: An easy ride among the palm trees on the edge of Marrakech, for beginners and experienced riders, with a guide from the stable.
s139: Calm horses, a guide who adapts to your level, and quiet tracks through the Palmeraie, with the Atlas on the horizon on clear days. Rides last one or two hours. A beach ride in Essaouira can also be arranged if you go there.
s144: Pickup, ride of one to two hours with a guide, mint tea, drive back.
s146: Float over the villages and fields north of Marrakech as the sun comes up over the Atlas. About one hour in the air, then breakfast in a Berber tent.
s147: A very early pickup takes you to the launch site outside the city. While the balloon is inflated you have tea; then you rise slowly to watch the sun light up the Jbilet hills and the snowy High Atlas. After landing, a traditional breakfast and a certificate. Flights are run by a licensed balloon company; we organise the booking and the transfer.
s148: Sunrise over the Atlas from the sky
s152: Pickup before dawn, flight, breakfast, back at your riad by late morning.
s153: Flights depend on the wind. If the pilot cancels, you choose another day or a full refund.
s154: Lake Ifni and Toubkal circuit, 6 days
s155: The big loop around the Toubkal massif. Remote valleys, Berber villages, a night by Lake Ifni and the summit at the end, when you are well acclimatised.
s156: Six days to really know the High Atlas. You leave Imlil eastwards to Tacheddirt, cross high passes into the quiet Ouarai valley, walk down to the village of Amsouzart and up to Lake Ifni, a turquoise lake closed in by rock walls. From there you cross Tizi n’Ouanoums (3,664 m) to the Toubkal refuge, and climb the summit on the last morning, better acclimatised than on any shorter trek. Mules carry the bags; you carry a daypack.

s162: Drive to Imlil, meet the team and walk over Tizi n’Tamatert to Tacheddirt, one of the highest villages of the valley.

s164: Climb to Tizi Likemt (3,555 m) and drop into the wide, quiet Ouarai valley.

s174: Imlil and Sidi Chamharouch day hike
s175: A real taste of the High Atlas in one day. Walk from Imlil through Aroumd to the shrine of Sidi Chamharouch, with lunch in a village house.
s176: Leave Marrakech in the morning and be walking in the mountains before 10. From Imlil the path climbs to Aroumd, the highest village of the valley, crosses the wide riverbed and follows the Mizane up to Sidi Chamharouch, a pilgrimage place built around a huge white rock. Lunch is tagine in a local house; back in Marrakech before dark.
s177: High Atlas in a single day
s181: Drive to Imlil, walk via Aroumd to Sidi Chamharouch and back, with lunch on the way. Drive back to Marrakech.
s183: Casablanca, Rabat, Meknes, Volubilis, Fes and Marrakech with a private driver. History, medinas and Roman ruins, at a calm pace.
s184: A private circuit through the four royal capitals of Morocco. You start in Casablanca with the Hassan II mosque, continue to Rabat, then Meknes and the Roman city of Volubilis, spend two full days in Fes, and end in Marrakech. Local licensed guides show you each medina; the driver handles the rest. Hotels or riads are chosen with you.
s185: Four royal capitals in one trip
s190: Airport pickup, Hassan II mosque and the Corniche.
s192: Hassan Tower, Mohammed V mausoleum and the Kasbah of the Udayas, then on to Meknes.
s194: Bab Mansour and the royal stables, the Roman mosaics of Volubilis, and Moulay Idriss, then Fes.
s196: A full day with a Fes guide: madrasas, tanneries and craftsmen.
s198: Free day, or an optional trip to Chefchaouen.

s201: Guided tour of the medina: Bahia Palace, souks, Jemaa el-Fna.
s205: Shop at the market, then cook a full Moroccan meal with a local cook. Salads, a tagine of your choice, bread and mint tea, and you eat what you make.
s206: A morning in the kitchen. You buy vegetables and spices with your host, learn which spice goes where, and cook step by step: cooked salads, a chicken or vegetable tagine, bread, and the right way to pour mint tea. You leave with the recipes and a full stomach.
s208: Cook and eat a full Moroccan meal
s211: Market shopping, cooking class, then lunch together.
s212: Your riad in Marrakech (transfer on request).
s214: An evening walk through the medina, eating what people in Marrakech actually eat. Msemen, harira, tangia, snail broth for the brave, and mint tea to finish.
s215: About ten tastings over three hours, in small stalls and family places away from the tourist menus. Your guide explains what you eat and how it is made, from the bread ovens to the tangia cooked slowly in the ashes of the hammam fire. Come hungry; vegetarians are welcome, just tell us.
s217: Places locals go, not tourist menus
s220: Start near Jemaa el-Fna, walk through the food streets with tastings, finish with mint tea.
s221: In front of the Café de France, Jemaa el-Fna.
s223: Half a day in the old city with a licensed guide. The Bahia Palace, the souks, the craftsmen’s quarters and Jemaa el-Fna, without getting lost or pushed into shops.
s224: The medina of Marrakech is easier and richer with someone who grew up in it. Your licensed guide starts at the Bahia Palace, walks you through the old Jewish quarter and the spice square, then into the souks of the dyers, metalworkers and leatherworkers, and ends at Jemaa el-Fna. You go at your pace; shopping only if you ask.
s229: Bahia Palace, the mellah, the souks and Jemaa el-Fna, with stops for mint tea.
s230: Your riad, or the entrance of the Bahia Palace.
s232: Over the Atlas to the Sahara. Aït Benhaddou, the Dades and Todra gorges, a camel ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes and a night in a desert camp.
s233: The classic desert journey from Marrakech. Day one crosses the Tizi n’Tichka pass and stops at the earth ksar of Aït Benhaddou before the night in the Dades valley. Day two follows the road of the kasbahs to the Todra gorge and on to Merzouga, where camels take you into the dunes for sunset and a night at camp. On day three you watch the sun rise over the sand and drive back to Marrakech. It is a lot of driving, but the landscapes change every hour.

s235: Night in a desert camp, sunrise on the dunes
s236: Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage site
s238: Marrakech, Tizi n’Tichka, Aït Benhaddou and Dades
s239: Cross the High Atlas by the Tichka pass (2,260 m), visit the ksar of Aït Benhaddou, then continue past Ouarzazate and the Valley of Roses to the Dades valley.
s240: Todra gorge and the Merzouga dunes
s241: Walk in the Todra gorge, then drive to Merzouga. Camels at sunset into the dunes; dinner, drums and the night at camp.
s243: Sunrise from the dunes, camel ride back to Merzouga, then the long drive to Marrakech, arriving in the evening.
s244: Shared tours travel in a minibus with other travellers. The private option is your own car and driver, and you can stop where you like.
s245: Desert nights are cold from November to March. Bring a warm layer.
s247: The shortest way to sleep in the desert from Marrakech. Aït Benhaddou, the Draa valley palm groves and a camel ride to a camp near Zagora.
s248: If you only have two days, Zagora is the realistic choice. The dunes are smaller than in Merzouga, but the road is beautiful: the Tichka pass, Aït Benhaddou, then the long palm valley of the Draa with its earth villages. You ride camels to the camp for dinner and a night under the stars, and drive back to Marrakech the next day.
s249: A night in the desert in just two days
s253: Over the Tichka pass to Aït Benhaddou, then through Agdz and the Draa valley. Camel ride at sunset to camp.
s254: Sunrise, breakfast at camp and the drive back to Marrakech.
s256: Morocco’s third-highest summit (4,071 m), from the green Aït Bouguemez valley. Long ridges, wide views and nights under canvas.
s257: The M’Goun is a huge whaleback ridge in the Central High Atlas, far from Marrakech and far from the crowds. You start in the Aït Bouguemez, the "happy valley", climb to the Tarkeddit plateau and reach the summit along a long ridge with views over half of Morocco. A trek for walkers who like space and silence.
s262: A long drive via Azilal into the valley. Short walk among the villages and fields.
s264: A steady climb out of the valley to the high plateau below the M’Goun ridge.
s266: Early start up to the ridge and along it to the summit, then back down to camp.
s267: Down the valley and back to Marrakech
s268: Walk down to the valley and drive back to Marrakech, arriving in the evening.
s269: Ourika valley and Setti Fatma waterfalls
s270: The green valley closest to Marrakech. A walk up to the Setti Fatma waterfalls with a local guide, a traditional Amazigh house and lunch by the river.
s271: One hour from Marrakech, the Ourika river cuts a green valley into the Atlas. You stop at a traditional Amazigh house to see how families live, then continue to Setti Fatma, where a local guide leads you on a rocky path up to the first of the seven waterfalls. Lunch is a tagine on a terrace over the river.
s276: Drive up the valley, visit an Amazigh house, walk to the waterfalls with a local guide, lunch and drive back.
s277: The path to the waterfalls is rocky and steep in places. Wear shoes with good grip.
s279: Morocco’s highest waterfalls, 110 m of water dropping into a green gorge. Walk down with a local guide, take a boat to the foot of the falls, meet the macaques.
s280: A full day out of the city, about two and a half hours north-east of Marrakech. A local guide walks you down the olive-shaded path to the bottom of the falls, where small boats go close to the spray, and back up the other side past Barbary macaques. Lunch with a view of the water, then the drive back.
s282: Boat ride to the foot of the falls
s285: Drive to Ouzoud, guided walk around and down to the falls, free time and lunch, drive back.
s286: Quad bike or buggy in Agafay or the Palmeraie
s287: Two hours on a quad or buggy through the palm grove or the stony hills of Agafay, with a stop for mint tea in a village.
s288: A short, fun outing for when you need a break from the medina. After a safety briefing and with helmets and scarves provided, you follow a guide on tracks through the palm grove or the Agafay hills. No licence needed; children can ride as passengers.
s289: Two hours of riding with a guide
s293: Pickup, briefing, two hours on the tracks with a tea stop, drive back.
s294: Tamatert and the three valleys, 3 days
s295: Village to village through the Imlil, Imnane and Ourika valleys. Guesthouse nights, terraced fields and easy-going mountain paths.
s296: The best trek if you want to see how people live in the High Atlas. You cross Tizi n’Tamatert from Imlil into the Imnane valley, then over to the upper Ourika valley, sleeping in family guesthouses. Walks are 4–6 hours a day on good paths, with tea stops in villages and views of the Toubkal peaks behind you.
s299: Good for families and first treks
s301: Drive to Imlil, then walk up to Tizi n’Tamatert (2,279 m) and down into the Imnane valley.
s303: A higher pass towards the Ourika valley, through shepherds’ summer pastures.
s305: A last morning walk down through the villages, then the car back to Marrakech.
s307: West of Imlil, over Tizi Mzik into the green Azzaden valley, to the highest waterfall of the Toubkal area.
s308: A varied loop on the quieter western side of Imlil. You cross Tizi Mzik into the Azzaden valley, sleep in simple mountain shelters and walk up past the shepherds’ huts of Tamsoult to the Ighouliden waterfall, which drops in several steps from the cliffs. Good for walkers who want real mountain views without going to the summit.
s311: Views of the Toubkal massif from Tizi Mzik
s312: Imlil, Tizi Mzik and Id Aissa
s313: Drive to Imlil, then climb through juniper to Tizi Mzik (2,489 m) and down into the Azzaden valley.
s315: Walk up to the summer pastures of Tamsoult and on to the Ighouliden waterfall. Picnic in the valley.
s317: Return over the pass to Imlil and drive back to Marrakech in the afternoon.
s319: The fast version of the Toubkal climb for fit walkers short on time. Up to the refuge on day one, summit and back to Marrakech on day two.
s320: An early pickup in Marrakech gets you to Imlil for breakfast, then you walk up the Mizane valley to the Toubkal refuge. The next morning you leave before dawn for the summit, come back to the refuge and walk down to Imlil, where the car waits to take you back to Marrakech. Two big days: choose this version only if you walk in the mountains regularly.
s321: Toubkal summit (4,167 m) in a weekend
s325: Early drive to Imlil, then a long climb through Aroumd and Sidi Chamharouch to the refuge. Lunch on the way, dinner and night at the refuge.
s327: Pre-dawn start to the summit, back to the refuge for a late breakfast, then down to Imlil and drive to Marrakech in the evening.
s328: Only for experienced walkers: you climb about 2,400 m in two days. If in doubt, take the 3-day trek.
s330: The classic ascent of North Africa’s highest peak (4,167 m) from Imlil, with a night in the village and a night at the refuge. Sunrise on the summit.
s331: This is the trek our guides walk more than any other. You leave Marrakech in the afternoon, sleep in a guesthouse in Imlil and set off the next morning up the Mizane valley, past the shrine of Sidi Chamharouch, to the Toubkal refuge at 3,207 m. On day three you start at 3 am with head torches and reach the summit around sunrise, then walk all the way down to Imlil and drive back to Marrakech for the evening. It is a real mountain day: long, steep in places and cold at the top, but no climbing skills are needed outside winter.
s332: Sunrise from the roof of North Africa
s333: The Mizane valley and the shrine of Sidi Chamharouch
s334: A night in a family guesthouse in Imlil
s335: Everything organised from Marrakech and back
s337: Afternoon drive into the High Atlas. Settle into the guesthouse, meet your guide and go through the plan for the next two days over dinner.
s342: A steady climb up the Mizane valley, with a rest near the checkpoint and lunch at Sidi Chamharouch. In the afternoon the path climbs to the refuge, where you sleep at 3,207 m.
s346: Sidi Chamharouch, about 40 minutes for lunch
s349: Toubkal summit and return to Marrakech
s350: An early start by head torch up the south cirque to the summit for sunrise. Back at the refuge for lunch, then down the valley to Imlil and the drive back to Marrakech.
s358: Your riad or hotel in Marrakech (or a nearby meeting point if cars can’t reach it).
s359: The summit day is long (about 9–10 hours of walking). Walking regularly in the weeks before helps a lot.
s360: From December to March the summit is under snow and the trip becomes a winter ascent with crampons. See our winter trip.
s361: Weather decides. If the guide judges the summit unsafe, you turn back. Your safety comes first.
s363: No. From April to November it is a walk on steep, rocky paths. You need good fitness and good shoes, not technical skills.
s364: Will the altitude be a problem?
s365: Most people feel the altitude above 3,500 m (short breath, mild headache). Going slowly, drinking a lot and sleeping at the refuge first help. Tell your guide how you feel.
s367: Toubkal under snow, with crampons and ice axe and a guide who knows the mountain in winter. Short initiation to snow techniques at the refuge.
s368: From December to March the High Atlas turns white and Toubkal becomes a real winter climb. The route is the same as in summer, but the slopes above the refuge are covered in hard snow, so you walk with crampons and carry an ice axe. On arrival at the refuge your guide checks the gear and practises the basics with you: walking in crampons, using the axe, stopping a slip. Days are shorter and colder, so the pace and the turn-back time are set by the guide.
s370: Crampon and ice-axe practice with your guide
s373: Morning drive to Imlil, then walk up the snowy Mizane valley to the refuge. Gear check before dinner.
s375: A morning of practice on the slopes near the refuge, then an acclimatisation walk if conditions allow. Early night.
s377: Early start in crampons to the summit, then the long walk down to Imlil and the drive to Marrakech.
s378: You need rigid or semi-rigid mountain boots that take crampons. Tell us your shoe size if you need to rent.
s379: Winter plans depend on snow and avalanche conditions. The guide may change the route or the day.
s380: How do I book a trip?
s381: Choose a trip, pick your date and the number of travellers, then send the request on WhatsApp or by email. We check availability and reply with the final price. Nothing is paid online.
s382: How quickly will I get an answer?
s383: Usually within a few hours on WhatsApp, every day of the week. In the mountains the network can drop for a while; we reply as soon as we are back in range.
s384: What is the difference between shared and private?
s385: On a shared trip you travel with other guests in a small group, which keeps the price low. A private trip is just you and your companions, with your own guide or driver and more freedom on timing.
s387: Small. The exact maximum depends on the trip and is confirmed when you book. Ask us if you want to know who else is on your date.
s388: How and when do I pay?
s389: Nothing is paid on this website. When we confirm your trip we send you the final price and how to pay. Ask us for a written quote first if you need one.
s390: What if I need to cancel?
s391: Tell us as early as possible on WhatsApp or by email. The conditions are on our cancellation page and confirmed with your booking. If we have to cancel for weather or safety, we offer you another date.
s392: Am I fit enough for Toubkal?
s393: If you can walk 6 hours on hills with breaks, you can usually reach the summit. The hard part is the long summit day and the altitude, not technique. Tell us about your experience and we will advise you honestly.
s395: Mountain treks are led by licensed mountain guides from the Imlil valleys. The guide decides on safety: if the weather or the group is not right for the summit, you turn back.
s397: Yes, we strongly recommend insurance that covers trekking up to 4,200 m and medical evacuation.
s399: Yes, many trips work well with children: day trips, Agafay, the three valleys trek, the desert. Toubkal summit is better for teenagers who already walk. Ask us about ages and child prices for your trip.
s400: What if my child gets tired on a trek?
s401: On village treks a mule can carry a tired child for part of the way. Tell us in advance so we plan for it.
s402: Can you handle vegetarian or other diets?
s403: Yes. Vegetarian is easy in Morocco: tagines, couscous and salads. Tell us about allergies or other diets when you book.
s404: Is the water safe to drink?
s405: Drink bottled or filtered water. In the mountains we fill bottles at springs and treat the water; bring a refillable bottle to avoid plastic.
s406: When is the best time to visit?
s407: Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–November) suit almost everything. Summer is great for the mountains and the coast, winter for the desert and the cities, and for a snowy Toubkal.
s408: What happens if the weather is bad?
s409: In the mountains the guide adapts the route or the day. If a trip cannot run safely, we offer another date; refund conditions are on our cancellation page.
